posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text:
Blogged about NYT/Siena.

I think we've "crossed the threshold." Polls project that Dems will win the Senate. They might be wrong, but that's what they project. No hiding from it tbh. https://t.co/TAn71UVSc1

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: The thing is, at this point, Dems can absorb a modest-sized polling error and win the Senate. Not a large one. But they have leads of >=3.0 points in states totaling 5 flips, plus in all their own seats.

posts.name: Dave Wasserman
posts.text:
Lots of fancy Texas early vote analyses out there, but here's a simple fact: in the 23 counties that voted for any statewide federal Dem this decade, early votes cast are at 91% of '24 levels. 

In the other 231 all-GOP counties, early votes cast are at just 79% of '24 levels.

posts.text: Dems already appear to be in good shape to grab a clear majority of governors, and the Rs look very shaky in Leans R kinds of races -- Florida, Kansas, Texas, and Vermont.

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text:
My current thinking:

GOP loses NC and OH Senate, though I’m not sure about OH.

GOP keeps AK, IA, KS, ME, and TX.

GOP flips MI.

GOP loses the House by 25 seats.

My Republican strategist friends believe I’m too optimistic and the GOP is now set to lose the House and Senate
